chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from al-Khadir ibn Abd al-Malik, from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the day in which there is doubt — for the people are alleging that whoever fasts it is at the status of one who breaks a fast during the month of Ramadan. So he said: They lied! If it was from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day for which he was given divine success, and if it was from other than it, then it is at the level of what has passed of the days.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status/level of — a juristic equivalence formula used by the Imam to clarify the legal standing of an act
key_terms.كَذَبُوا: They lied — the Imam's strong rejection of a false popular belief, indicating that fasting the day of doubt carries no sin
key_terms.وُفِّقَ: Given tawfiq (divine success/guidance) — indicates spiritual blessing and reward from God
key_terms.يَوْمُ الشَّكِّ: Day of Doubt — the last day of Sha'ban when there is uncertainty about the sighting of the Ramadan crescent moon

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the day of doubt (yawm al-shakk) between Sha'ban and Ramadan according to Imam al-Kazim?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Hakim reports asking Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) about the ruling on fasting the 'day of doubt' (yawm al-shakk) — the last day of Sha'ban when it is uncertain whether the new moon of Ramadan has been sighted. Some people held the view that fasting such a day would be equivalent to breaking a fast in Ramadan, which would be a grave sin. The Imam firmly refuted this claim, stating that if the day turns out to be Ramadan, the person receives the full reward; and if it belongs to Sha'ban or another month, it counts as a voluntary fast just like any other day — so there is no spiritual harm in either case.
word_analysis: for which he was given success/blessed

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Al Khizr Bin Abdul Malik, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the day in which there is a doubt, so the people are alleging that the one who Fasts it would be at the status of the one who breaks a Fast during the Month of Ramazan’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are lying! If it was from the Month of Ramazan, so it would be a fortunate day for him, and if it was from others, so it is with a status of what has past from the days’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from al-Hadramiy ibn ‘Abd al-Malik from Muhammad ibn Hakim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a day about which people have doubts. People think if one fasts on such a day, it is like destroying one day of fasting in the month of Ramadan. He (the Imam) said, ‘They have spoken a lie. If it is of the month of Ramadan, it is a fortunate chance for him; and if it is of other days then it is like any of the past days.’”
